Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates diffuse, dense, nodular opacities predominantly in the upper lobes (right > left) along with extensive calcification of the diaphragm and pleura. This pattern of metastatic pulmonary calcification, specifically involving the upper lobes and associated with soft tissue/vascular calcifications, is characteristic of chronic renal failure (secondary hyperparathyroidism).
